block.name: TractionControlLevel
block.notes: TractionControlLevel=({float}0.06, {float}0.16} *****New to PC2*** Note TractionControlGrip= TractionControlLevel= The first one is the 'aggressiveness' of the traction control system (how much wheelspin is allowed before TC engages). Forgive me but I can't specifically remember whether it's a higher value that allows for more wheelspin or a lower one... I believe (and only believe) that higher values mean the traction control system engages LATER, with lower values allowing the traction control to kick in earlier. The second value is the strength of the traction control. There are two values - the first is the strength on the LOW setting, the second is the strength of the HIGH setting. Essentially it's about balancing the numbers. If you have a car with low power at pretty much anything but peak revs, lower the efficiency to allow for smoother clutch engagement (0.79 in my case), make sure only low traction control is allowed on launch, and then balance the TractionControlGrip and TractionControlLevel figures. If you want a smooth launch without too much traction control interference, set the TC GRIP level to a lower number (0.5, for example, to allow it to kick in earlier) as well as setting the TC LEVEL to a low number (in my case, 0.07) - this essentially meant that the TC kicked in early to keep the car pointing straight and true on launch, but the low LEVEL meant it only had a slight effect.

block.name: BrakeCriticalTemp
block.notes: Critical brake temperature (uint32 variant). V2.1 calls this "BrakeTorque (min)" — WRONG. Values 200-1200 = temperatures, not torque. Binary chain: follows BrakeMaxTemp (100%) → precedes BrakeWearRate (84%) / BrakeFailure (16%). 4-corner field: 2000 hits = 500 files × 4 corners. WARNING: this hash also appears with marker 0x22 (float) in some files — see BrakeCriticalTemp_Float.

block.name: BrakeMaxTemp
block.notes: Maximum brake operating temperature (uint32 variant). Also known as "BrakeFadeRange" in V2.1 — both names mean the same thing: the temp ceiling beyond which brake fade becomes severe. Binary chain: follows BrakeFadeEnd (99%) → precedes BrakeCriticalTemp (100%). 4-corner field: 1980 hits = 495 files × 4 corners (20 files use 0x20 marker). WARNING: this hash also appears with marker 0x22 (float) in some files — see BrakeMaxTemp_Float.

block.name: BrakeTempRange
block.notes: [SPECULATIVE] Brake temperature range compound (min_temp, max_temp). V2.1 says (min_temp, max_temp). Suffix 52 is exotic — not in standard table. Binary chain: follows BrakeDiscInertia/BrakeWearRate → precedes BrakeFadeStart (100%). 4-corner field: appears 2000 times = 500 files × 4 corners. Suffix variants: 52 90(888), 52 C2(480), 52 50(318), 52 F4(244), 52 2C(272), etc.

block.name: BrakeFadeStart
block.notes: Brake fade start threshold — fraction of optimum temp where fade begins. Binary chain: follows BrakeTempRange (100%) → precedes BrakeFadeEnd. Example: 0.34 (PC2), 0.55 (typical AMS2), 0.75 (high-perf).

block.name: BrakeFadeEnd
block.notes: Brake fade end threshold — fraction of optimum temp where fade is total. Binary chain: follows BrakeFadeStart → precedes BrakeMaxTemp (99%). Always higher than BrakeFadeStart.

block.name: BrakeFailure
block.notes: BrakeFailure compound (failure_rate, severity). NOTE: corpus mostly uses exotic suffix "22 0A" (1960/2000 = 98%) which also reads as float,float. Standard suffix A2 used in 40/2000 files. Both produce the same field types. Note: suffix "22" is exotic — not a standard float suffix here. Binary chain: follows BrakeWearRate (84%) or BrakeCriticalTemp (16%) → precedes BrakeTorque. 4-corner field: 2000 hits = 500 files × 4 corners.

block.name: BrakeTorque
block.notes: BrakeTorque — max brake torque (float variant). WARNING: This hash appears with BOTH 0x22 (float) and 0x21 (uint32) markers. 22 = float (some files) 21 = uint32 (most files — e.g. 3000, 4250 for Ligier JS2R) Binary chain: follows BrakeFailure → precedes BrakeHeating. 4-corner field: 1980 hits = 495 files × 4 corners.

block.name: BrakeTorque_Int
block.notes: BrakeTorque — max brake torque (integer variant, marker 0x21). Same hash as BrakeTorque but different marker (uint32 instead of float). User-confirmed: Ligier JS2R = 3000. Corpus sample: 4250. Binary chain: same position as float variant.

block.name: BrakeDuctCooling
block.notes: BrakeDuctCooling — duct-based brake cooling coefficient. New in AMS2. V2.1 translation wrongly calls this "BumpTravel" — CONFIRMED brake field. Binary chain: follows BrakeCooling (100%) → precedes BrakeHeatParam1 (92%). 4-corner field: 1708 hits = 427 files × 4 corners. Absent (0x28) in 73 files.

block.name: BrakeHeatParam1
block.notes: [SPECULATIVE] Brake thermal parameter 1 — possibly heat capacity or thermal mass. Values ~2.69-2.91 across most cars. Higher for heavy cars (up to 4.4). Binary chain: follows BrakeDuctCooling (93%) → precedes BrakeHeatParam2 (100%). 4-corner field: 2000 hits = 500 files × 4 corners. V2.1 has this as unnamed h_02e4826c.

block.name: BrakeHeatParam4
block.notes: [SPECULATIVE] Brake thermal parameter 4 — last brake field before next section. Very small values (~1.3e-06 to 2e-06). Possibly residual heat dissipation rate. V2.1 translation wrongly calls this "BumpTravel" — CONFIRMED brake field. Binary chain: follows BrakeCooling2 (100%) → followed by 0xE0 section marker (76%). 4-corner field: 1840 hits = 460 files × 4 corners. Absent (0x28) in 40 files. --- Note (unrelated): when using road car chassis to make a race car, automatic tire selection will not work unless you change the first footer byte from 2F to 35.

block.name: BrakeHeatParam2
block.notes: [SPECULATIVE] Brake thermal parameter 2 — possibly thermal conductivity or radiation factor. Values ~0.26-0.31 for most cars, up to 0.71 for high-performance. V2.1 translation wrongly calls this "ReboundTravel" — CONFIRMED brake field. Binary chain: follows BrakeHeatParam1 (100%) → precedes BrakeCooling2 (100%). 4-corner field: 2000 hits = 500 files × 4 corners.

block.name: BrakeCooling2
block.notes: [SPECULATIVE] Secondary brake cooling compound — speed-dependent cooling. V2.1 identifies this as BrakeCooling (2 of 2) with (base_rate, speed_factor). Suffix A2 = float, float. Has 9 suffix variants (A2 34 most common at 1158). Binary chain: follows BrakeHeatParam2 (100%) → precedes BrakeHeatParam4 (100%). 4-corner field: 2000 hits = 500 files × 4 corners.
